messages:
tara: Quick follow-up from the onboarding RFC — we're seeing a class of quantized wheels that pass the unit smoke but fail the bench sampling with weird tokenization timing spikes. Anyone seen this pattern before?

alex: Which stage fails? full microbench run or the lightweight preflight?

tara: The lightweight preflight (the 1k-slice) shows 3x tail latency compared to float baseline for some sequences. Full bench eventually smooths out but that still worries the SLOs.

maria: Do we have a repro input? Could be kv-cache interaction with the kernel layout. Also check if the quantized binary used per-layer fused kernels (we saw that with newer VC builds).

tara: I attached a small trace in the ticket but quick repro: short prompt + many single-token replies. It seems to blow up when seq_len grows past cached prefix threshold.

ranjit: Sounds like an execution edge: quantized runtime might be doing a fallback to slower matmul for certain attention sizes. Would be good to capture which kernel names are being invoked. Any chance to log kernel signatures during preflight?

ben: We currently restrict preflight to a sandboxed runtime that doesn't expose kernel names for security reasons. But we can add an opt-in verbose flag for eng-ml to capture runtime traces. :wrench:

maria: Another angle: our ingest validator treats quantized images as blackbox and only asserts functional parity on a small golden set. Maybe expand the golden set for cache-bound patterns (many short replies).

tara: I worry about coupling too much to gold inputs — that becomes brittle. Instead propose we split onboarding into two lanes: "fast acceptance" (lightweight functional + perf guardrails) and "deep validation" (full bench + kernel tracing + optional num-sensitiveness tests). Fast acceptance should allow canary-serving but limit QPS.

alex: I like lanes. For fast acceptance we need stricter interface contracts: manifest should include kernel capability hints (e.g., supports-prefetch, kv-popcount) so router can choose compatible runtime. That avoids surprises at serving time.

ranjit: Agree. The manifest hints don't need to be exhaustive but should capture fatal incompatibilities. We should version the hint schema and bake a fallback policy so older manifests still work.

ben: Implementation note: ingest pipeline already computes a minimal meta blob. We can add a compact "execution-quirks" field. Example: `{supports_kv_cache: true, fused_attn: "v2", max_prefetch_len: 1024}`.

maria: +1 but let's make those values categorical not free text to avoid parsing errors. Also we need a validator test that asserts the runtime honors the declared limits (e.g., reject models that advertise max_prefetch_len=4096 but blow up at 2048).

tara: Operationally, rollouts should use the lanes: fast-accepted models go to canary pool with traffic caps and observability enabled (latency diff alarms), deep-validated models can join dedicated pools.

bench-bot: bench-runner: quick-preflight completed for model xq-1q8. Results: functional OK, perf-sample median=23ms, p95=210ms (guard 150ms).

alex: bench-bot shows the p95 breach. For now block auto-promote to prod. Can we auto-trigger deep validation on p95 breach?

ben: We can. Add a rule: if p95 > guard then enqueue deep-validator job (kernel trace + expanded bench). Should also attach the manifest and runtime hints.

maria: One more tradeoff: deep validation is expensive (GPU/time). Let's prioritize models by estimated impact (embedding size, expected traffic). We have cost signals in registry.

tara: Good. Action items: 1) Add "execution-quirks" schema PR (ben + alex), 2) add opt-in runtime kernel tracing flag for preflight (ben + ranjit), 3) implement lane state machine and auto-enqueue rule for p95 breaches (tara + maria). I'll open the follow-up RFC with proposed JSON schema and workflow.

alex: If you want, I can draft the router fallback policy to honor manifest hints.

tara: Please do. Aim for minimal change to routing logic — prefer route-by-compat then by latency tier.

maria: I'll sketch the expanded golden sample set for cache-bound patterns and add it to the onboarding playbook.

ranjit: I'll prototype kernel-trace capture in the sandboxed runtime this week.

ben: Will start the schema PR and add a test to the ingest pipeline.

tara: Thanks all. Let's sync in the onboarding sync next Wed. :thumbsup:
